src/Daoris.Desktop/Daoris.Desktop.Driver.why: a lower bound on a delay the session itself waits out in real time (the go-on goes a quiet period after the work ends); a loaded machine waits longer, never less, so it cannot flake, and the session has no clock seam to move
the queue's rate cap is a count over a span (at most sixty frames a second); load only widens the span the frames are stamped over, so the relation cannot fail on a slow machine

the claim is the watch's own debounce cap, a bound of the product measured in a Process test beside a real file watcher; the bound is also said in the output line, and no seam moves the watcher's clock
the deadline is a count per second of the loop's real time (at most one a second and one more); load only lengthens the elapsed time, so the count it bounds cannot be over it

a bench at scale: a change laid over the kept list must cost less than reading the whole list and stay inside its budget; the measured operation is the behaviour, run alone as a Process test, and the line it writes says both times

a lower bound: the store waits the five seconds its design says before it refuses a busy write; a loaded machine waits longer, never less, and the wait is SQLite's own busy timeout, which no clock seam moves
a bench at scale: the session list over a large home must stay inside its budget, the operation's own time and not this test's; run alone as a Process test
a bench at scale: a session's opening, alone and four at once, must stay inside its budget over a real repository; the operation's own time is the behaviour, run alone as a Process test
the claim is that a pin is not made to wait out the lock a clearing holds, a wait of real time inside the settings store's lock that no seam moves; without it the pin would pass after the wait
the claim is the watch's own debounce, a bound of the product measured in a Process test beside real git; the time is said in the output line, and no seam moves the watcher's clock
